gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 12 build gate now runs the landed nvme PCI starter beside the phase12 surveys so the complex-driver lane stays reviewable in one bounded path.

The shared Phase 12 make target now runs the nvme PCI starter beside the survey gates for the tranche's other complex-driver lanes, which keeps this survey checkpoint reviewable through one bounded entry point.

The first bounded starter is now landed around a lab-only queue planner that validates queue geometry, computes DMA page demand, assigns monotonic queue identifiers, tracks doorbell offsets, and now also records PRP buffer-shape, PRP metadata, and recovery replay summaries without claiming live PCI behavior.

Dedicated driver tests now keep the starter honest around admin and I/O queue planning, DMA page rounding, invalid geometry rejection, reset-time queue freeze behavior, the PRP buffer-shape helper, the PRP metadata helper, and the recovery replay helper.

The slice note records what the landed queue planner, PRP buffer-shape helper, PRP metadata helper, and recovery replay helper cover so the survey can focus on the remaining roadmap gap instead of re-explaining the starter surface.

The landed virtio_net probe snapshot starter now gives the broader Phase 12 tranche a second real complex-driver foothold, which helps compare the nvme PCI lane against another bounded driver starter instead of only against survey scaffolding.

The landed virtio_scsi queue-layout starter gives the Phase 12 tranche a third real complex-driver foothold, which makes the nvme PCI survey more honest about current peer progress and keeps future runs from treating nvme as the only driver with a starter.
A dedicated survey gate is the smallest truthful way to record that the current nvme PCI starter has landed while the deeper transport and DMA roadmap work remains intentionally incomplete.

The lane needs an archival note that compares the current starter against the roadmap's segmented-rollout rule so future runs do not mistake the queue planner, PRP helpers, and recovery replay helper for a production PCI port.

The bounded nvme PCI packet includes one tiny PRP buffer-shape helper that records first-page offset, rounded span, PRP tail-page count, and PRP list bound checks without crossing into live PRP list construction, request submission, or hardware-backed queue setup.

The landed PRP metadata helper now quantifies command-inline data pointers, PRP-list-covered pages, extra descriptor DMA footprint, total DMA bytes, and reset-time descriptor rebuild need without claiming live PRP allocation, DMA mapping, or queue submission.

The landed recovery replay helper now reports reset-generation staleness for cached PRP metadata, admin-queue replay need, dropped I/O queue rebuild count, and post-reset queue numbering without claiming live timeout recovery, IRQ handling, or hardware-backed reset transport.

The roadmap's DMA-safe abstractions requirement is still blocked because Host Memory Buffer policy, real PRP or SGL DMA mapping, and live PCI queue creation still need a transport-safe substrate beyond the now-landed queue-planning, PRP buffer-shape, PRP metadata, and recovery replay helpers.

The roadmap's throughput and recovery parity requirement is still blocked because blk-mq queue_rq flow, IRQ-driven completion polling, timeout recovery plumbing, and suspend or resume parity still sit beyond the current bounded starter.
